Summary (auto): Kickoff technical integration for Sidereal Systems marketplace listing and a small quant pilot to measure cost/latency. Discussed KMS, VPC, Helm packaging, canary routing, onprem connector, and benchmarks. Agreed action items.

[00:00:12] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we-- uh-- we wanted to run through the onramp checklist and then scope a small quant pilot for the connector. I'm Maya, I'll own the commercial side but Liam and Priya will run the tech bits.
[00:00:34] Carlos: Thanks, Maya. Happy to be here. We have a tight timeline for our marketplace listing, target end of month, so want to make sure nothing blocks.
[00:00:49] Liam: Great, Carlos. Quick note, when we say "marketplace listing" for Redwood, we mean the packaged connector + reference ref-arch and the listing manifest - the thing that lets customers deploy via the cloud partner marketplace, correct?
[00:01:08] Anya: Yup. We need the Helm chart, a sample values.yaml, and the VPC peering / private link doc, plus KMS compatibility notes. Also audit logs requirements.
[00:01:24] Priya: That's right. We'll provide a template values and a lightweight helm chart that uses our operator. For on-prem we have a slightly different flow but same packaging concept. Note, sometimes the transcript shows 'Helm chard' ha.
[00:01:42] Michael: Quick question on data residency - some of our customers require keys stay in their HSM. How does Redwood handle key wrapping in that scenario?
[00:01:55] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments. For the hosted listing we can document KMS passthrough patterns and key wrapping. Priya, maybe you can explain the current KMS integrations?
[00:02:12] Priya: Sure. For Private we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS and customer HSM via KMIP in the onprem bundle. For the marketplace listing we'll include a runbook: "How to point Redwood Dedicated to your KMS". Caveat: some customers need custom key wrapping - that's an ops note.
[00:02:39] Carlos: We will need the runbook. Also can you confirm audit log formats? Our security team ingests JSON structured logs into Splunk.
[00:02:51] Liam: We'll share the audit schema. Quick aside: our runtime emits token-level telemetry and request traces; for marketplace we can toggle retention windows. It's often misread as "token level telemitry" in exports.
[00:03:10] Anya: On network patterns - we prefer VPC peering rather than public egress. Is there a private link option for your hosted control plane?
[00:03:22] Jordan: Yes, we have private control plane options for Dedicated and Private modes. For marketplace we document both private link and peering patterns, but the actual connector install can be configured to use a NAT or a VPC endpoint.
[00:03:38] Ravi: For our on-prem bundles we'll be behind a strict firewall, so need clear egress rules. Also curious about the connector's resource profile - how many GPUs or vCPU for a tiny dev cluster?
[00:03:53] Priya: For the pilot we recommend a minimal node pool: 1x A100-equivalent for inference or 4 vCPU / 32GB RAM for smaller CPU-runtime tests. But depends on model. We'll provide a perf table.
[00:04:12] Michael: That brings up the quant pilot - what's the scope? We want to see cost reduction but not degrade the quality too much.
[00:04:22] Liam: Exactly. Pilot proposal: run the same workload on your test tenant with baseline FP16 (or FP32) and then test int8 quantized variants using Redwood's quant profiles. Measure latency p50/p95, token cost delta, and quality degradation on a small evaluation prompt set.
[00:04:45] Carlos: Sounds good. How invasive is the quant flow - do we need to retrain or only run post-training quant?
[00:04:55] Priya: It's post-training quantization with calibration; no retrain required for most of our supported models. Some model families need per-channel calibration. We'll note which are safe.
[00:05:09] Maya: A small doc note - we'll include a "safe list" of models for auto-quant. We should also call out kernel compatibility - some older kernels don't support the optimized int8 paths.
[00:05:25] Anya: Kernel compatibility is critical. We run a mix of GPU types across regions. How does Redwood detect and select kernels?
[00:05:34] Liam: Our runtime does kernel selection and will choose optimized ops at runtime based on device capabilities. For the pilot we'll pin a kernel profile for the bench to keep results comparable. There is sometimes weirdness where transcribe shows "kernel selection as kettle" but just ignore that.
[00:05:53] Carlos: For the marketplace manifest, do you require us to publish images to your registry or can we reference our own container registry? Some security rules disallow external registries.
[00:06:05] Jordan: You can host images in your registry; the chart supports imagePullSecrets and private registries. For the marketplace listing we'll include a manifest that references a public ECR or your private ECR with instructions on granting read access to the deployer account.
[00:06:22] Michael: Good. Can we talk about canary routing and fallback - we want predictable degradation, not total failover.
[00:06:32] Priya: Our rollout supports canary with traffic weights and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant. For the listing we can include sample policies: e.g., 5% canary for 1 hour, monitor perf, then 50%/100%. We'll share example config.
[00:06:49] Carlos: On benchmarks - we want synthetic load but also a replay of real traffic. Is there a way to replay token sequences and KV cache warmup?
[00:07:00] Liam: Yes, we will work with you to capture a sanitized trace and replay it. Important to capture typical sequence lengths for realistic batching behavior - otherwise batching numbers look great but latency is off. Also note KV cache warmup matters for chat sessions.
[00:07:20] Anya: Re: batching - can you expose batching windows? Some customers prefer low latency so they'll want small batching windows.
[00:07:29] Priya: We will expose batching config in the values.yaml. For marketplace default we choose workload-aware batching that keeps p95 under your SLO, but the helm chart allows overriding.
[00:07:42] Michael: Any licensing or redistributable constraints on the connector? We may want to rebrand parts for our docs.
[00:07:52] Jordan: The onprem bundle is under the Redwood partner license; we provide a small rebrand-friendly README and sample legal blurb for the marketplace listing. We'll send the license text.
[00:08:03] Carlos: Okay, actionables - we need the checklist and a working pilot plan. Who owns what?
[00:08:11] Maya: We'll capture that. Quick note: we sometimes see names reversed in transcriptions so I'll repeat: Maya (AE), Liam (SE), Priya (SE), Jordan (Partner Eng) are owning the Redwood tasks.
[00:08:23] Carlos: Sidereal side: Carlos, Anya, Michael, Ravi.
[00:08:29] Liam: For the bench run we recommend 4 experiments: baseline FP16, int8 post-quant, minimal cpu runtime, and a canary config with smaller model. We'll produce a CSV with p50/p95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:08:46] Anya: Can we also measure memory footprint to validate packing across GPUs?
[00:08:52] Priya: Yes, memory and VRAM utilization will be in the perf outputs. Also will include KV cache hit stats.
[00:09:04] Michael: About telemetry - how granular is the tracing? We want to link traces to our observability pipeline.
[00:09:12] Liam: We emit request-level traces and token aggregates; we can forward to your OTLP endpoint or S3 bucket of traces for the pilot. For enterprise installs we set up push to your SIEM.
[00:09:28] Carlos: Security review: do you have SOC2 and ISO info? Our procurement team will request it before listing goes live.
[00:09:37] Maya: Yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II reports and our security whitepaper. Also we'll share an architecture diagram and the audit log schema.
[00:09:49] Ravi: For network egress, can we get a minimal allowlist? We'll prefer to whitelist IP ranges.
[00:09:58] Jordan: We'll share a short allowlist for the instrumented control plane endpoints and the storage endpoints. For marketplace, recommend peering when possible.
[00:10:09] Anya: Edge case - our customers in APAC want a private deployment; how does the marketplace listing support region-specific onprem installs?
[00:10:20] Priya: The chart is region agnostic; the listing will document region-specific variables and a matrix of supported cloud regions. For onprem we provide an air-gapped option with an offline bundle. We'll include that in the README.
[00:10:36] Michael: One more ops question - upgrades. How do we coordinate rolling upgrades without traffic loss?
[00:10:44] Liam: The helm chart supports rolling updates with preStop hooks for draining in-flight requests; for model rollouts we use canary + traffic mirroring to validate. We'll share an upgrade playbook.
[00:10:58] Carlos: Cool. Anything else on the listing manifest?
[00:11:03] Maya: We'll add sample tags, a marketing blurb, and minimal screenshots. But Sidereal will need to approve copy.
[00:11:12] Anya: We'll own copy approval.
[00:11:16] Maya: Alright, quick timeline recap: Maya sends checklist by 9/16, Priya & Liam to produce quant profiles and helm example by 9/18, Sidereal provisions test tenant by 9/20, bench session targeted 9/23. Is that okay?
[00:11:33] Carlos: Yes that works.

[00:11:41] Priya: We have a small smoke harness and a set of sanity prompts. We'll share a link to a repo and a short runbook.
[00:11:51] Ravi: For the runbook, include steps for setting KMS and how to rotate keys safely during the pilot.
